item.title: Michigan Wolverines fend off shocking upset bid from Western Michigan in early season thriller
item.description: Michigan football nearly relived its Appalachian State nightmare as Western Michigan led 12-7 before Bryce Underwood's 46-yard Hail Mary saved the day.
item.content:encoded:
We just passed the 19th anniversary of Michigan's shocking upset loss to Appalachian State that opened their 2007 season.

Well, we came about as close as you can to another major Michigan upset to kick off this year.

The Wolverines got their slate underway on Saturday night at Michigan Stadium by welcoming the Western Michigan Broncos.

THE 2007 MOUNTAINEERS REMAIN COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S GREATEST 'WHAT-IF' STORY NEARLY TWO DECADES LATER

As is often the case in these Week 1 matchups, Michigan came into this one as an overwhelming 27.5-point favorite.

Oddsmakers were also looking at a fairly high-scoring game with the o/u set at 49.5.

However, this turned into a low-scoring, defensive battle, with Michigan opening the scoring when QB Bryce Underwood punched it into the end zone from the 1-yard line.

A few minutes later, the Broncos answered with a field goal, then tacked on another before halftime, and that was the end of the scoring in the first half.

OREGON RALLIES FROM SLOW START, THWARTS BOISE STATE'S UPSET BID IN SEASON OPENER

The teams went to the locker room with Michigan up just 7-6.

That was a stunner, but surely Michigan would come out firing and put the 2025 MAC champions away.

Nope.

The next time either team would score wasn't until the fourth quarter, when Western Michigan kicked their third field goal of the game to go up 9-7.

Both teams failed to score on their next drives, but with Michigan looking like they were on the verge of at least marching downfield for a late game-winning field goal, the Broncos pulled off a stunner.

Western Michigan's Joshua Franklin managed to punch the ball out of Underwood's grasp as he fell to the turf, with the Broncos pouncing on top of it.

DEION SANDERS TAKES MULTIPLE SWIPES AT HIS CRITICS AFTER COLORADO STUNS GEORGIA TECH

Despite a scare due to a fumble of their own, the Broncos hung on to the ball and added another field goal to go up 12-7.

On the ensuing drive, Underwood connected with receiver Channing Goodwin around midfield, and with no timeouts, the Wolverines scrambled to the line of scrimmage to spike the ball with just nine seconds on the clock.

On the final play of the game, Underwood found space and gave his receivers time to get downfield before heaving a bomb that ended up sailing just out the back of the end zone.

But Michigan caught a break. Upon review, it was found that there was still one second left on the clock.

It was a controversial call, to say the least. Prepare to hear plenty of talk about it this week. The decision left just enough time for the Wolverines to get a snap off, with Underwood connecting with JJ Buchanan for a touchdown and a 13-12 Michigan win.

That 46-yard beauty of a Hail Mary for the win was the last of Underwood's 170 passing yards. He also rushed for 46 yards and one touchdown.

That's a maiden win for the Kyle Whittingham era in Ann Arbor, and surely no one saw it looking like that.

A heartbreaker for the Broncos and a heart-stopper for Michigan.

We're barely into the college football season, and we already have a classic (with a bit of controversy mixed in to boot).

Things will not get any easier for the Wolverines, as their next game will be on Sept. 12 when they welcome the No. 10 Oklahoma Sooners to the Big House.

item.title: California pizza joint allegedly used as meth distribution hub as illegal immigrant charged
item.description: Kawal Preet Singh allegedly used a Round Table Pizza in Dinuba to distribute over 40 pounds of methamphetamine as part of an organized crime network.
item.content:encoded:
A California pizza shop allegedly had far more than pies on the menu, with a man accused of using the Round Table Pizza restaurant to sell massive quantities of meth.

Kawal Preet Singh, a 50-year-old Indian national living illegally in the United States, was indicted Thursday on federal drug and firearm charges after authorities allegedly uncovered more than 40 pounds of methamphetamine, three guns and over $10,000 in cash.

Federal prosecutors say Singh operated the Round Table Pizza restaurant in Dinuba, a Tulare County city about 30 miles southeast of Fresno, and used the business to distribute large quantities of methamphetamine.

CALIFORNIA SUSPECT'S ALLEGED $30K METH STASH SEIZED AFTER HE LEFT BACKPACK IN RIDESHARE: POLICE

Singh pleaded not guilty during his arraignment Thursday. He is not in custody, according to The Fresno Bee.

The Dinuba restaurant is listed as permanently closed on Google.

"The employee involved in the reported incident had worked at this location for approximately one and a half months," the company told GV Wire.

Erin Mandzik, senior director of corporate communications for FAT Brands, Round Table Pizza’s parent company, told The Fresno Bee that the restaurant was independently owned and operated.

Mandzik said the local owners had no knowledge of the alleged illegal activity before it came to light and were fully cooperating with authorities, according to the newspaper.

Fox News Digital reached out to Round Table Pizza seeking additional information about Singh’s role, the restaurant’s ownership and the decision to permanently close the location.

FEDS SEIZE MOUNTAIN OF FENTANYL FROM 'OPEN-AIR DRUG MARKET' IN MASSIVE CRACKDOWN TARGETING GANG CREWS

Federal agents searched Singh’s home and the restaurant Aug. 18 as part of an investigation into Indian organized crime in California’s Central Valley, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California.

Investigators allegedly found approximately 13.8 kilograms, or more than 30 pounds, of suspected methamphetamine at Singh’s home, The Fresno Bee reported.

CBP OFFICERS SEIZE OVER $2.8M IN COCAINE AND METH IN BACK-TO-BACK BUSTS AT CALIFORNIA PORT OF ENTRY

Another roughly 4.9 kilograms, or nearly 11 pounds, was allegedly packed into five clear plastic bags inside Singh’s Hyundai Sonata parked at the restaurant, according to the newspaper.

Agents also seized a semiautomatic handgun and $11,800 in cash, the outlet reported.

NEVADA MAN FUNNELED 140 GUNS TO VIOLENT MEXICAN DRUG CARTELS, INCLUDING POWERFUL 'MILITARY-STYLE' RIFLES: DOJ

Photographs released by the Justice Department showed two handguns allegedly seized during the investigation, including one with a teal-colored frame. Another image showed clear plastic bags containing a crystalline substance authorities identified as methamphetamine.

A federal grand jury charged Singh with distribution of methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.

MEXICAN MAFIA TURNED AMERICAN NEIGHBORHOODS INTO ‘GANGSTA’S PARADISE’ WITH MURDERS, KIDNAPPINGS, DRUGS: FEDS

The investigation reportedly began with a May tip about a suspected narcotics trafficker operating in Fresno and distributing controlled substances.

Investigators later received information about a trafficker known as "Camy," who was described as a Sikh Indian man involved in long-haul trucking, according to court documents cited by The Fresno Bee.

BORDER AGENTS UNCOVER $20M COCAINE STASH HIDDEN BENEATH TRUCK FLOORBOARDS IN MASSIVE BUST

"The information identified the narcotics trafficker as ‘Camy’ and described him as a Sikh Indian male involved in long-haul trucking," an FBI affidavit said, according to the outlet. "The suspect worked with a network of other Sikh Indian truck drivers to transport narcotics."

Investigators developed evidence indicating that a network of truck drivers transported hundreds of kilograms of cocaine from Mexico into the United States for an unidentified Mexican cartel, The Fresno Bee reported. Singh has not been charged with a cocaine-related crime.

The Central Valley High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Task Force later identified Singh as a subject of the investigation, federal prosecutors said.

Search warrants signed Aug. 13 covered Singh, his home and the Dinuba restaurant, according to The Fresno Bee. Five days later, agents allegedly watched Singh leave the restaurant and drive to his home before searching both properties.

Singh allegedly told investigators he had not sold methamphetamine for approximately two months and claimed he was storing the drugs for a friend, according to the outlet.

Singh faces at least 10 years in federal prison if convicted of the drug charges. The firearm count could add at least five more years behind bars.

Prosecutors emphasized that the charges are allegations and that Singh is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

Singh’s next federal court hearing is scheduled for Nov. 4.

item.title: Kennedy Center ceiling partially collapses as Trump-led board pushes for 2-year closure
item.description: Photos show a partial ceiling collapse in a main Kennedy Center hallway, which officials say underscores the urgent need for Trump-backed renovations.
item.content:encoded:
The Kennedy Center shared photos on Saturday that showed a partial ceiling collapse that happened during a rainstorm in the main hallway of the over 50-year-old performing arts building.

Roma Daravi, vice president of public relations for the Kennedy Center, said the collapse underscored the need to close the building for renovations.

"Another example of the urgent need to close for renovation and revitalization, as our Chairman President [Donald] Trump has championed," Daravi said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital, adding, "This structural failure stems from decades of neglect and deferred maintenance by the previous leadership, and there’s no justification for further delays in restoring America’s cultural center."

VIDEO EXPOSES DISREPAIR LURKING BENEATH TRUMP KENNEDY CENTER AS $257M RENOVATION LOOMS

The center’s board, which is led by Trump, voted in August to close the building for two years.

This came after a judge ruled in May that Trump’s name must come off the building months after the board voted to name it: "The Donald J. Trump and The John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts."

"Unless I am free to do what I do better than anyone else, bring this Institution back, physically, financially, and artistically, I have no interest in continuing what could only be a hopeless journey into 'NEVER NEVER LAND,'" Trump wrote on Truth Social at the time. "Therefore, based on the fact that the Radical Left Democrats care more about opposing your favorite President, ME, than saving a dying Performing Arts Center, almost all of which lose large amounts of money throughout the Country, we are going to be working with Congress to transfer this failing Institution back to them so they can make a determination as to what to do with it."

TRUMP'S NAME TO BE REMOVED FROM KENNEDY CENTER AS APPEALS COURT DENIES BOARD'S REQUEST FOR ADMINISTRATIVE STAY

Last month, the board voted to rename the institution’s grounds "President Donald J. Trump Plaza" and to put lettering on the building that says "The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump."

The board remains in court fighting to move forward with the name changes, as well as the closure and $250 million in renovations.

Grace Terpstra, founder of the community group Keep the KC, which is fighting the closure, said she thinks the board will use the collapse "to make the point that the whole thing needs to be shut down, that it’s going to fall on everybody."

KENNEDY CENTER DISPUTES ALLEGATIONS ON CONTRACTOR BIDS DESPITE DEMOCRAT SENATOR'S CLAIMS

She added, "I think they’ll try to make it into a bigger thing and show that they’ve found a lot of other things."

A tarp and scaffolding has covered the front of the building since the bronze letters that made up Trump’s name were removed in June.

Last week, the center did remove a piece of modern artwork called "Blue" that has been outside the building since 2019, saying in a statement, "we are honored to have been stewards" of the late sculptor Joel Shapiro's work.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Oregon rallies from slow start, thwarts Boise State's upset bid in season opener
item.description: Dante Moore threw for 388 yards and three touchdowns as No. 2 Oregon rallied past Boise State in a tense 34-27 season opener at Autzen Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
No. 2 Oregon survived a scare in its first game of the 2026 college football season Saturday. Despite entering the opener as heavy favorites over unranked Boise State, the Ducks found themselves tied 27-27 in the fourth quarter.

But the Ducks ultimately held off a resilient Broncos team when wide receiver Dakorien Moore hauled in a 62-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Dante Moore, putting Oregon ahead for good.

Oregon held on to win 34-27 and extend its home winning streak against nonconference opponents to 39 games, the longest active streak in the nation.

WHAT IS TARGETING? COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S MOST CONTROVERSIAL RULE, EXPLAINED

Boise State quarterback Maddux Madsen finished with 181 passing yards and three touchdowns. Despite Saturday’s loss, Madsen delivered the kind of performance he can potentially build on this season after throwing for 2,334 yards and 18 touchdowns last year.

The Broncos, who join the rebuilt Pac-12 Conference this year, went 9-5 last season in the Mountain West.

Boise State scored on the first series of the game, with Madsen hitting Cam Bates with a 13-yard scoring pass to cap an 11-play drive. The Ducks tied it on Jordon Davison’s 1-yard dive early in the second quarter.

After Evan Stewart muffed a punt and the Broncos recovered, Sire Gaines scored on a 37-yard reception to give Boise State the lead again. Canaan Moore added a 29-yard field goal to extend it with less than three minutes left before halftime.

With just 19 seconds left, Dante Moore found Jamari Johnson with a 27-yard pass to close the game to 17-14 at the break.

MEET JOSH HOOVER: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT NEW INDIANA STAR QUARTERBACK

After Gage Hurych’s 26-yard field goal, Oregon went ahead on Jeremiah McClellan’s 8-yard TD catch. But the Broncos tied it up again before the end of the third quarter on Madsen’s 7-yard scoring pass to Matt Wagner.

Hurych and Canaan Moore traded field goals in the fourth quarter before Dakorien Moore’s touchdown.

Oregon travels to Stillwater next week to face Oklahoma State. Boise State will host Memphis in Week 2.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Machete-wielding MS-13 gangster wanted for murder walks free after Biden-appointed judge releases him: DHS
item.description: A convicted MS-13 killer known as "La Bruja" or "the witch" is free in California after a federal judge ruled ICE held him without a required bond hearing for five months.
item.content:encoded:
An MS-13 gang member convicted in a savage execution-style murder is out of federal custody in California after a federal judge ordered his immediate release, igniting fury from the Trump administration.

U.S. District Judge Jinsook Ohta ordered the release of David Antonio Aviles Perez, 35, aka "the witch," after finding that immigration officials held him for five months without giving him a bond hearing or determining whether he posed a danger to the public or a flight risk.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin accused the Biden-appointed judge of putting the public in danger by ordering Aviles Perez’s release.

DHS EVISCERATES MEDIA FOR ‘ABSOLUTE ABSURDITY’ OVER CONCERN ABOUT ‘WORST OF THE WORST’ ACTIVIST JUDGES LIST

"This radical activist judge has put American lives at risk by releasing a wanted murderer," Mullin said in a statement Saturday.

"This is now the SECOND time this dangerous illegal has been released back onto the streets in California," he added. "Because sanctuary politicians want to play politics from the bench, innocent Americans are in danger."

SANCTUARY LAWS COULD STOP POLICE FROM PROTECTING KIDS. SO WE’RE SUING CALIFORNIA

The case centers on a brutal 2014 gang killing in El Salvador and a legal fight over the Trump administration’s authority to detain immigrants while removal proceedings unfold.

Alvise Perez, identified by Salvadoran prosecutors as an active MS-13 member also known as "La Bruja," or "The Witch," was convicted while outside El Salvador in December 2025 and sentenced to 20 years in prison for aggravated murder.

ICE NABS ACCUSED MS-13 KILLER HIDING IN NORTHERN VIRGINIA SUBURB

Prosecutors said Aviles Perez and another MS-13 member chased a man through a mountainous area in La Unión before fellow gang members forced the victim to stop and kneel.

The victim was held by the shoulders as Aviles Perez and his accomplice approached, prosecutors said.

The gang members then shot the man in the chest, back and face before fleeing. Both defendants were tried and convicted while outside the country.

Aviles Perez entered the U.S. at an unknown date and location, according to DHS.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH BRUTAL SLAYING ONE DAY AFTER CALIFORNIA JUDGE RELEASED HIM: DHS

He was arrested in Monterey, California, in 2023, after allegedly swinging a machete at a homeless man at Laguna Grande Park near Monterey State Beach. He allegedly hid the weapon before officers recovered it from a nearby Holiday Inn parking lot.

Aviles Perez was charged and convicted after the incident but later released from custody. DHS blamed California’s sanctuary policies, which limit cooperation between local authorities and federal immigration officials.

DHS BUYS TWO CALIFORNIA MIGRANT DETENTION CENTERS FOR $1.5B TO BOOST ICE DEPORTATION CAPACITY

ICE agents arrested him again in San Diego on March 26 and took him into custody pending his removal to El Salvador.

He was held at the Otay Mesa Detention Center pending removal to El Salvador until Ohta ordered his immediate release Aug. 26, federal court records show.

After nearly five months in immigration custody, Aviles Perez filed a petition challenging his detention and seeking his immediate release.

Ohta ruled that immigration officials violated his Fifth Amendment due process rights by holding him without an individualized assessment of whether he was dangerous or likely to flee.

"Although Petitioner appears to have previously been convicted following a fight with another individual in May 2023, the government has offered no evidence that it detained him after considering those facts and making an individualized determination of his danger to the public or flight risk," Ohta wrote.

FEDERAL JUDGE IN NEW YORK TIES TRUMP ADMIN HANDS ON ARRESTS AT IMMIGRATION COURTS

The judge said federal officials gave Aviles Perez "no process before or after his detention" and had not shown that providing a hearing would place an undue burden on the government.

Ohta ordered his immediate release and barred ICE from detaining him again unless an immigration judge first holds a bond hearing and determines that renewed detention is warranted.

A status report was filed in the case Aug. 27, one day after the release order. DHS said Aviles Perez was subsequently released from federal custody.

The ruling did not clear Aviles Perez of wrongdoing or find that he posed no danger. It focused on whether immigration officials followed the required process to justify keeping him detained.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom appointed Ohta to the San Diego County Superior Court in December 2020, according to the governor’s office.

BIDEN JUDGE TORCHES TRUMP ICE CRACKDOWN AS ‘DEVOID OF RATIONAL EXPLANATION,’ NUKES COURTHOUSE ARREST POLICY

President Joe Biden nominated her to the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California in September 2021. The Senate confirmed her that December, and her judicial commission was issued later that month, according to the Federal Judicial Center.

Mullin vowed that the ruling would not derail the administration’s immigration crackdown.

"DHS and ICE will not be deterred by these partisan games," he said. "If California’s leaders won’t protect Americans, DHS will."

Fox News Digital reached out to Ohta's office for additional comment and confirmation surrounding Aviles Perez’s release.

item.title: Trump-linked MAGA Inc pours $10M into Ken Paxton's Texas Senate race against James Talarico
item.description: MAGA Inc. drops $10 million in ads backing Ken Paxton against James Talarico in a neck and neck Texas Senate race that could reshape the midterms.
item.content:encoded:
MAGA, Inc., the super PAC linked to President Donald Trump, has made its first major midterm buy with $10 million in ad spending to support Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in his Senate race, according to a new filing with the Federal Election Commission.

Paxton and Democrat state Rep. James Talarico are locked in a tight race in which polls continually show the two candidates neck and neck.

The $10 million will go toward digital and TV ads across the state.

FOX NEWS POLL: GOP DIVISIONS SHAPE TEXAS SENATE RACE

Trump’s endorsement earlier this year already helped Paxton beat incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the Republican primary.

"While James Talarico has a record of raising taxes on working families, my Protecting the Texas Promise Agenda cuts costs and makes life more affordable. Thank you, President @realDonaldTrump, for your support," Paxton wrote on X on Saturday while sharing a post about the ad buy. "Together we will win for Texas and America."

The decision comes after weeks of speculation over whether the super PAC would put money into the hotly contested race.

Talarico’s campaign also responded to the move, telling Fox News Digital, "Billionaire-backed dark money groups are lying about James Talarico because they’re scared of the people-powered movement we’re building to fix this broken, corrupt political system."

BERNIE SANDERS DEMANDS DEMOCRATS BAN SUPER PACS FROM PRIMARIES, BLASTS AIPAC, ‘CORRUPT SYSTEM’

Talarico, who has called for higher taxes on the wealthy, called out billionaires heading to the Republican midterm convention starting Wednesday.

"Next week, billionaire mega-donors and their puppet politicians will gather at a convention in Dallas to clink champagne glasses and toast their own corruption," he said. 

"They’re paying $20,000 for entry to a Billionaire Ball celebrating corrupt tariffs, billionaire tax breaks, and a new forever war that are all driving grocery costs through the roof. We’ll be doing something different. We’re bringing Republicans, Democrats and independents together to collect groceries for our neighbors who have been screwed over by corrupt politicians."

Calling him "High Tax Talarico," MAGA Inc. spokesperson Alex Pfeiffer told Fox News Digital the Democrat "wants to take money out of Texans' pockets. MAGA Inc. is going to ensure Texas knows about Talarico's radical policies and elects Ken Paxton to the U.S. Senate."

TALARICO’S ‘PROUD CAPITALIST’ ABOUT-FACE COLLIDES WITH RESURFACED CALL TO ‘DISMANTLE’ CAPITALISM

Talarico’s campaign has raised $72 million since the campaign began, mostly from small donors, compared to $16.8 million by Paxton’s campaign, according to the Texas Tribune.

The two anti-Talarico ads slam his policies on taxes and rural hospitals while touting Paxton’s support for doubling the child tax credit, allowing tax breaks for medical expenses and a $50,000 deduction for first-time homebuyers.

MAGA, Inc. has around $400 million in campaign funds, which Trump called "my money" while speaking to reporters this week, adding, "I’m going to spend whatever amount of money necessary to try and help us."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Tennessee Volunteers fans pay incredible tribute to Dolly Parton during season opener
item.description: All 102,000 fans at Neyland Stadium sang Dolly Parton's "I Will Always Love You" in unison as Tennessee football honored the late country icon.
item.content:encoded:
The death of country music, movie, theme park and, frankly, all-around icon Dolly Parton hit a lot of people hard.

That includes folks in her home state of Tennessee, a place she was virtually synonymous with.

On Saturday, the Tennessee Volunteers football team opened its 2026 season, and the entire Neyland Stadium crowd paid tribute to the late legend.

PEYTON MANNING PAYS TRIBUTE TO DOLLY PARTON: 'TENNESSEE WON'T BE THE SAME WITHOUT HER!'

It was announced ahead of the game that one of the tributes to Parton — an orange butterfly decal with her name on it — would be on the back of every Volunteers player's helmet.

Head coach Josh Heupel revealed that the decal will be sticking around all season long.

"All that she's meant across the world, this country, and certainly the Queen of East Tennessee," Heupel said, per ESPN. "A lady that was extremely proud of her roots. You look at her impact, just her ability to give back, make an impact to people, certainly here in East Tennessee. She means a lot to people across this country, but certainly here inside the state of Tennessee, too."

The Volunteers hosted the Furman Paladins on Saturday, and there were more tributes on the way during the game.

Perhaps the biggest came when the entire stadium — 102,000 fans strong — joined together to sing Parton's 1974 hit "I Will Always Love You" in unison.

Probably more than a few people in the stands were cutting onions during that one.

What a moment.

But there was more. For the last couple of seasons, the Vols have played the Morgan Wallen song "The Way I Talk" during the fourth quarter.

TENNESSEE MOVES TO RENAME NASHVILLE AIRPORT FOR DOLLY PARTON DAYS AFTER BELOVED ICON'S DEATH

This time? Dolly's "My Tennessee Mountain Home."

It wouldn't be a shocker to see this become a new tradition, and just another example of how much Dolly Parton meant to the state of Tennessee.

item.title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers hopes to be 'supporting my pregnant wife' by next year after final NFL season
item.description: Aaron Rodgers told Mad Dog Sports Radio he hopes to have a pregnant wife by next year as he prepares for life after what may be his final season.
item.content:encoded:
Next Sunday will mark the beginning of what could be Aaron Rodgers’ final NFL season. The four-time league MVP signed a one-year contract during the offseason to return to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Rodgers’ potential retirement has been widely discussed, and more details emerged this week about what his life could look like beyond football.

Starting a family appears to be among the 42-year-old quarterback’s priorities whenever he does decide to step away from the game. Rodgers told SiriusXM that he hopes he and his wife will be in the midst of doing so by this time next year.

STEELERS LEGEND JEROME BETTIS SAYS THERE'S 'EXCITEMENT IN THE AIR' AS AARON RODGERS RETURNS FOR FINAL SEASON

"I'm hopefully going to be supporting my pregnant wife because we're going to start a family and I am not going to be making a lot of appearances or statements," Rodgers told SiriusXM's "Mad Dog Radio."

"And I’m looking forward to a life of quiet after 22 years in the pros and three in college and getting my body healed up and working on a family. That’s what I’m looking forward to."

The conversation then turned to whether Rodgers was simply looking ahead or hinting at something more immediate. "I’m talking about I’m hoping that I have a pregnant wife by next [year] this time," Rodgers said.

After a period of distance from some relatives, Rodgers acknowledged that reconnecting with them had influenced his hopes of starting a family. Rodgers added that he's enjoyed spending time with his brother’s children.

AARON RODGERS CREDITS WIFE FOR FAMILY REUNION AFTER MORE THAN A DECADE OF ESTRANGEMENT

"I'm definitely excited about it," Rodgers said. "I mean, being back in my family's lives, I'm having a lot of fun being Uncle Aaron. I have a few godkids that I'm involved with, but being Uncle Aaron to my brother's kids has been a lot of fun."

"And the more I'm around them, the more I get excited, and so does the wife, about having some of our own," he continued. "So, I'm excited for that. I can't wait for that next chapter of life and all that that entails, and sleepless nights and crying babies and changing diapers and all those things, I'm looking forward to all of it."

Since announcing his marriage, Rodgers has kept his wife’s personal life out of the spotlight. The NFL star has described his spouse as a "private person."

item.title: Fan runs onto field at Houston Cougars game, gets absolutely trucked by police officer
item.description: A fan who rushed the field during the Houston Cougars’ 33-20 win over the Oregon State Beavers was leveled by a police officer with a textbook tackle.
item.content:encoded:
The college football season, in all its glory, is upon us, and it feels like it couldn’t have come soon enough for all of us.

In fact, a lunatic in Houston couldn't wait more than one game before sprinting onto the field.

Unfortunately for him — but fortunately for the rest of us — he was absolutely demolished by a police officer who was at the top of his game.

HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL

The No. 23 Cougars opened their season with one of the tougher Week 1 matchups, with the Oregon State Beavers coming to town.

Houston ended up winning 33-20 to go 1-0 in this young college football season, but they didn't get the job done before some dude in a blue shirt hopped on the field to... actually, I'm not really sure what he was trying to accomplish.

UMASS PLAYER ABSOLUTELY OBLITERATES UNSUSPECTING WOMAN ON THE SIDELINES AFTER INTERCEPTION

Jeez! That's some top-notch work from the boys in blue.

I think Houston’s going to get calls asking how many more years of eligibility that cop has left because that tackle was textbook.

I still don't understand why people do this. Sure, you get a few moments of fleeting face time on social media, but at what cost?

Legal problems?

Expulsion?

Getting driven through the Earth's crust by a cop or security guard who definitely played at least a year or two of college ball?

INDIANA'S MASCOT STARTS THE SEASON WITH AN ABSOLUTE HEATER THAT PUTS OTHER MASCOTS TO SHAME

Well, he'll be feeling that one tomorrow, and probably for several days after.

I'm sure he's not thinking about doing that again, but on the off chance that he is, the next time the Cougars are in action will be on Sept. 12, when they host the Southern Jaguars.

The following week, they'll have what is shaping up to be a huge game for the Big XII championship picture when they travel to Lubbock to take on Texas Tech.

item.title: Dr Phil says Lindsay Clancy mistrial a 'teachable moment' on postpartum psychosis: 'There was a failure here'
item.description: Dr. Phil McGraw calls the Lindsay Clancy case a "psychiatric emergency that wasn't treated as such" and warns of a potential copycat effect.
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Phil McGraw on Saturday weighed in on the Lindsay Clancy trial, one day after the judge declared a mistrial when the jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict in the killings of her three children.

The defense team of the mother who admitted to strangling her three children to death in 2023 claims the 36-year-old was suffering from postpartum psychosis and wasn’t in control of her actions when she killed her children.

McGraw told Fox News anchor Aishah Hasnie on "Fox News Live" Saturday that Clancy's children — Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months — "are the real folks we need to give our attention to here. Three innocent children did lose their lives, and you can never explain these situations away simply."

PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL

He said it also concerns him when mental illness gets depicted in the courtroom, it becomes "kind of a political, ideological football that’s used to try to skew something or is kind of debunked by another side rather than looking at what actually took place."

McGraw stressed that there eventually will be "accountability" in the case. Even if she’s not found criminally responsible, "she’s not going home."

"She’s going to have to live with this the rest of her life and probably in a psychiatric facility if, in fact, she is not guilty by reason of mental defect or disease," he said.

"I think people underestimate the power of psychosis in taking over someone’s life. It’s not an excuse, but, for example, if she had a brain tumor you could see on an X-ray, people would go ‘OK, I get that.’ And when you have what took place here, it could be just as powerful as someone whose brain is hijacked by a tumor.

LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY

"I’m not excusing what she did in any way," he said. "I think she should be held fully accountable, but I think we need to understand causation."

The prosecution made a "pretty clunky presentation," McGraw said, adding that he felt they got their act together "in the end."

"I’ve spent a lot of my professional career working in trial sciences and dealing with juries and juries looking for a coherent explanation," he explained.

He said the defense’s explanation was "much more understandable and much more coherent than what the prosecution did.

McGraw also worried that the case could cause a "copycat" effect.

"We certainly don’t want that to take place here, so we need to look at what the cultural effects are," he said. 

There is also a "huge" difference between postpartum depression and postpartum psychosis, he stressed.

ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY

"Postpartum psychosis is a psychiatric emergency that requires immediate hospitalization," he said. "It’s not a time to adjust medications. It’s not a time to schedule an extra appointment during the week. It is a psychiatric emergency that requires in-patient care and separation from the children. Not tomorrow morning, not tomorrow afternoon, but immediately."

He called Clancy’s case a "psychiatric emergency that wasn’t treated as such."

It’s one thing to use the case as a "teachable moment for the country," McGraw cautioned, but it’s another for people to raise her up as some kind of "heroine."

"There’s nothing to be celebrated here," he said. "If there’s any lesson to be taken for our culture, it’s that there was a failure here. This was a woman who asked for help. She admitted herself to the hospital. Was that enough?"

The jury "tends to get it right," he said, explaining that they were "headed toward committing her for a long period of time."

"I think people need to understand that mental illness is a serious, serious issue," he said, adding he was worried that people would forget about Cora, Dawson and Callan.

ROGAN SHREDS SUPPORTERS OF LINDSAY CLANCY, SAYS THEY WOULDN'T RALLY IF A FATHER WERE ON TRIAL FOR SAME CRIME

"I hate we are focusing everywhere except there," he said. "And there are a lot of fingers to point, but now’s not the time to do that. We need to adjudicate this case, and then we need to step back and say, ‘What can we learn from this?’

Situations like Clancy’s case "occur one or two times out of 1,000," McGraw explained, "but that’s not nothing. One or two times out of 1,000 are one or two times too many. This is avoidable."

His wish is that people would pay attention to the "red flags" depicted in Clancy’s case that can be "internalized to help mothers when they get in over their heads and need the kind of intervention that was needed here."

"Reach out for help," he urged. "It’s not weakness. It’s strength."

item.title: In-N-Out's popular burger style started with a customer request decades ago
item.description: In-N-Out's Animal Style burger traces back to the early 1960s, when a customer spotted an associate's custom creation and asked for one just like it.
item.content:encoded:
In-N-Out Burger is known for its simple menu, with basic burgers, fries and shakes. Yet by 2005, the fast-food chain was listing some of its most popular off-menu orders on a "Not-So-Secret Menu" online.

Among the most famous off-menu offerings is the Animal Style burger, which the company website says is a "burger of your choice with hand-leafed lettuce, tomato, a mustard-cooked beef patty; add pickle, extra spread, with grilled onions."

In-N-Out’s website says the restaurants accommodate special orders because they’re "all about making our customers happy," and that’s just how the Animal Style burger got its start.

AMERICA'S FAVORITE FAST-FOOD CHAIN NAMED: MCDONALD'S WINS HEARTS BUT NOT BEST BURGER, SURVEY SAYS

"We began serving the Animal Style burger in the early 1960s when a customer watched one of our associates make his own customized burger and asked for one made the same way," In-N-Out Burger Chief Operating Officer Denny Warnick told Fox News Digital.

"The name was created there on the spot. Over the years, many of the variations in preparation for our basic menu items were given names, usually by the customers who frequently ordered their burgers that way. The terms were merely used to describe a way of preparing an order or a menu item exactly the way a customer wanted it."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Warnick said some of those names stuck, and, today, many customers order from the "secret" menu.

"Whether a ‘secret menu’ order or not, we still cook every burger fresh-to-order, exactly how the customer wants it," he said.

In addition to Animal Style, In-N-Out includes on its off-menu list Double-Meat with two beef patties; the 3x3, with three beef patties and three slices of American cheese; the 4x4, which is the same as the 3x3 but with an added patty and cheese slice; the Grilled Cheese, which replaces a burger patty with two slices of American cheese; and Protein Style, which is "your favorite burger wrapped in hand-leafed lettuce instead of a bun."

Founders Harry and Esther Snyder opened the first In-N-Out in a suburb of Los Angeles in 1948. According to the company’s website, it was California’s first drive-thru hamburger stand.

By 1973, there were 13 restaurants open, all in Los Angeles County.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Today, the company is still privately owned by the Snyder family, and there are more than 400 locations in 10 states.

The off-menu options have been an open secret for decades.

The Los Angeles Times reported in 2004 that In-N-Out customers had known about ordering their burgers Animal Style "for years."

"Relish the not-so-secret menu," the Times advised in 2005, noting that customers could find the secret menu on In-N-Out’s website and suggesting they try their burgers Animal Style and fries well done.

"Then try to find the little Bible verse references hidden in the wrappers and stamped under the cups, a fun game if you’re trying to sober up from an evening out," the Times added.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Though Animal Style is well known by now, the special burger is still attracting new converts.

"Got my burger Animal Style for the first time," a Redditor wrote on a subreddit two years ago. "It honestly was a game changer and is my new order. I don’t think I will ever go back."

"From LA. My parents have been going to [In-N-Out] long before I was born, and they just learned about Animal Style a month ago," another user responded. "I couldn’t believe my frickin ears."

Another off-menu order not listed on In-N-Out’s online menu is the Flying Dutchman — two patties and two cheese slices without buns or condiments — which the company says on its history page was created by former CEO Guy Snyder before he died in 1999.

item.title: Somehow, the Miami Hurricanes have done it again with yet another Heisman-level quarterback
item.description: Darian Mensah's dominant debut at Miami continues a stunning pattern as Mario Cristobal lands yet another elite transfer portal quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
I remember it like it was yesterday.

January 13, 2024. I was at a friend's birthday party with a group of fans representing each of the "Big 3" Florida schools (Miami, Florida, and Florida State).

Being a Gator fan, I was relishing in joining my fellow Florida fanatics and Seminole supporters mocking the Miami contingent that they had whiffed on all their quarterback targets in the transfer portal.

ACC SUPREMACY: IS IT REALLY THE MIAMI HURRICANES VERSUS THE FIELD FOR THE 2026 SEASON?

As we laughed and reveled in their misery, a notification flashed across everyone's phone screen that changed the tide of the night in favor of the Canes fans.

"BREAKING: Cam Ward, the ex-Washington State QB, heading to Miami."

ONE OF THESE EIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS WILL BE HOISTING THE NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TROPHY IN 2026

The Hurricanes had found their guy, but after a Heisman-level season in 2024, their one year rental was off to the NFL Draft.

So Miami's rivals fired up the trolls once again, and towards the end of the portal period, it looked like the Hurricanes were going to have to eat crow.

That is, until they plucked Georgia quarterback Carson Beck from the ranks of the NFL Draft.

Then the Canes rode another late transfer pickup to within a quarter of winning the national championship.

So when Miami and Mario Cristobal were without a signal caller heading into the teeth of the offseason, we all knew better than to gloat.

And that proved to be the right decision, as the Canes once again persuaded an NFL Draft hopeful - this time Duke transfer Darian Mensah - to hop in the boat in Coral Gables.

UCLA QUARTERBACK ATTEMPTS TO EXPLOIT LOOPHOLE IN TRANSFER PORTAL WINDOW WITH UNIQUE TACTIC

Mensah was given a king's ransom to make his way down to South Florida, and so far, though it's only been one game, that investment is looking to be paying dividends.

I think I speak for the rest of college football when I ask: how do the Canes keep doing this?

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S AP TOP 25 IS OUT: WHO’S OVERRATED, UNDERRATED AND FLAT-OUT SNUBBED?

I'm reminded of the famous scene from "Breaking Bad," when Aaron Paul's character screams "HE CAN'T KEEP GETTING AWAY WITH IT!"

Granted, Miami played a Stanford team that was missing half its roster due to injury and probably isn't much to write home about even when fully healthy.

But those numbers would look good in a 7-on-7 scrimmage, let alone in a conference game on the road three time zones from home.

Mensah looked as good as the numbers suggested, too, ripping NFL-level throws and distributing the ball to his myriad playmakers, namely wide receiver Malachi Toney.

Somehow, some way, Cristobal and the Canes have another quarterback who can realistically win the Heisman trophy and lead them on a deep Playoff run.

The schedule for Miami won't offer a ton of resistance either; there will be far more Stanford-level teams than Playoff-caliber ones.

When you combine all that and Mensah's skill with the weapons he's been surrounded with (not to mention elite offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson), the Hurricanes might be here to stay.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Let this be a warning to any rival fanbase rooting on the downfall of Miami (I include myself in that).

If the offseason starts to drag on next January and they still haven't signed a quarterback, don't hit send on that X post with all the laughing emojis.

Chances are they are a few calls away from landing a potential first-rounder looking to give college one last go.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: FBI's fifth Most Wanted Fraudster captured after alleged SNAP scam suspect arrested in India
item.description: Manjit Singh Bedi was arrested in India after allegedly fleeing the U.S. to escape SNAP benefits fraud charges tied to an alleged $600,000 EBT scheme.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters initiative notched its fifth arrest in just three months after authorities in India arrested Manjit Singh Bedi Friday, and the bureau is working to return the alleged SNAP benefits fraud suspect to the United States, Fox News Digital has learned.

The FBI worked with Indian authorities to secure Bedi's arrest and is actively working to return him to the U.S. to face charges, according to the bureau. 

Bedi's arrest is the fifth through the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters initiative, which targets fugitives accused of major financial crimes.

Launched in June, the initiative has led to the arrests of five fugitives whom the FBI says are collectively accused of more than $2 billion in alleged fraud after spending nearly 4,000 combined days on the run.

FBI NABS ALLEGED $547M MEDICARE FRAUD FUGITIVE OVERSEAS, THIRD CAPTURE FROM 'MOST WANTED FRAUDSTERS' LIST

FBI officials say the latest arrest underscores the bureau's effort to pursue alleged fraudsters who fled overseas in an attempt to evade prosecution.

"Five Most Wanted Fraudsters captured in just three months is a historic success for this initiative," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital.

"The days of taking advantage of American taxpayers without consequence are over."

Federal investigators allege Bedi defrauded the U.S. government out of at least $600,000 through a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme between March 2024 and June 2025, while operating an Asian grocery store in Tacoma, Washington.

EXCLUSIVE: FBI ADDS ALLEGED COVID FRAUDSTER ACCUSED OF TAKING $5M FROM KIDS' MEAL PROGRAM TO MOST WANTED LIST

According to the FBI, Bedi swiped SNAP recipients' Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards, gave them cash instead of eligible food purchases and kept roughly half of the benefits for himself.

After being indicted on wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud charges, Bedi was ordered to surrender his passport and remain in Washington state while awaiting court proceedings, according to the FBI.

Investigators allege he instead drove across the Canadian border before fleeing to India. A federal arrest warrant charging him with violating the conditions of his release was issued on May 21, 2026.

The FBI had offered a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to Bedi's arrest and conviction. The bureau said the naturalized U.S. citizen was believed to be living in India before his arrest.

"As this arrest in India shows, the Justice Department's reach extends to every corner of the planet," Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division told Fox News Digital.

"The Fraud Division will continue to work hand-in-hand with the FBI to ensure fraudsters like Bedi are held accountable, no matter where they hide."

item.title: Former Pentagon AI chief warns Flock cameras could create 'China-like surveillance state' in the US
item.description: Former Pentagon AI Policy Director Mark Beall warns Flock cameras could create a "China-like surveillance state" without strict court oversight.
item.content:encoded:
Former Pentagon AI Policy Director Mark Beall warned that expanding artificial intelligence surveillance tools, like Flock cameras, could turn American communities into a "China-like surveillance state" unless guardrails are enforced.

Speaking on "Saturday in America," Beall argued that while this technology can have vital law enforcement benefits, clear rules and judicial oversight are necessary to protect the rights of Americans at home.

"We have to be careful that we don't go too far to the other direction and create a China-like surveillance state, which is literally what AI capabilities will ultimately enable and are enabling right now," Beall told Fox News.

TEENS ACCUSED OF DESTROYING FLOCK CAMERA UNTIL BATTERY EXPLODED, IGNITING FIRE NEAR HOMES: REPORT

From destroyed camera poles to viral signs blocking surveillance lenses, some communities are pushing back against neighborhood surveillance cameras. Flock cameras are automated license plate readers used by law enforcement to record vehicle data that can aid criminal investigations. People in communities with the cameras have raised concerns about privacy and potential misuse by law enforcement.

Beall acknowledged that the technology can benefit law enforcement but said people’s privacy concerns are also valid. He urged a compromise and called for guardrails on how the cameras can be used, including strict rules and court oversight to prevent officers from abusing the technology for personal reasons.

FLOCK SAFETY CAMERAS NEED CONSTITUTIONAL GUARDRAILS BEFORE FURTHER DEPLOYMENT, TENNESSEE MAYOR ARGUES

"It’s tough to bring the message of compromise to the American people, especially when it comes to our constitutional protections," Beall said.

"I think what we're seeing across the board when it comes to artificial intelligence is that the innovation upside is so tremendous, but across all of these different use cases, including the Flock cameras, what we really need are strong guardrails, a strong policy that allows us to maintain those special values, the American founding principles that make this country so great," he added.

FLOCK SURVEILLANCE SPREADS ACROSS THE SOUTH AS RED-STATE LAWMAKERS SEEK TO AX '1984'-STYLE TRACKING TOOLS

Lawmakers from both parties have raised similar concerns and called for rules governing the surveillance technology. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., has proposed banning the technology outright, and Rep. Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., has pushed to cut federal funding for local installations.

In Florida, transportation officials have ordered law enforcement agencies to take down the license plate readers from state highways. They cited privacy concerns and reports of misuse of the technology.

DAVID MARCUS: CHINA TRIP A GLIMPSE INTO THE SURVEILLANCE STATE AMERICA MUST NEVER BECOME

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis criticized the cameras at a news conference Monday, saying, "If you want to get in your car, and you want to go down to Buc-ee's in St. Augustine, it's really none of the government's damn business if you're doing that, right? What we don't want in the state of Florida is to have a digital AI surveillance state where everything we're doing is being tracked at all times."

He added the technology has sometimes been useful but questioned where the data is going and how it is being stored.

"They claim that the companies aren't going to misuse it, but no one's watching that, and I know you can make some money selling cameras, but you really can make a lot of money if you can sell people's data," DeSantis said.

THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Flock Safety said it announced new safeguards, including cutting default data retention to seven days, making misuse detection mandatory for every customer and calling on the broader surveillance industry to meet those same standards.

In August, Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley addressed privacy and safety concerns in an interview with Fox News host Kayleigh McEnany.

"When people talk about just one of these, privacy or safety, they're prioritizing the wrong thing, and what we have to prioritize as a country is compromise," Langley told Fox News. "How do we have our safety, and how do we balance privacy?"

EX-INDIANA DEPUTY CHARGED WITH FELONY FOR ALLEGEDLY USING FLOCK CAMERAS TO STALK GIRLFRIEND

He said the company is focused on ensuring the technology is used for good, including by recommending seven-day data retention limits and holding those who misuse the system accountable.

"Today, it is too often that in Flock and in other technologies, there's no regulation. There's no accountability, and we think that's wrong," Langley said.

"We announced changes that required auditing, that required using our audit assistance tool, which detects abnormal behavior, and we're calling on state regulators to focus less on banning this type of technology and more [on] holding our law enforcement community accountable."

item.title: Christie Brinkley shares how she keeps her three adult children coming home
item.description: Christie Brinkley reveals how she keeps all three adult children coming home and why losing both parents deepened her devotion to family time.
item.content:encoded:
Christie Brinkley never really had to face an empty nest.

The actress and supermodel stars opposite Steve Guttenberg in "American Summer," a feel-good tribute to simpler times and family connections. 

The 72-year-old told Fox News Digital those themes aren't just on-screen. They're values she's embraced in her own life, creating a home her three adult children can still return to.

The movie, which hit theaters Sept. 4, follows Guttenberg's character as he looks back on a formative childhood summer filled with baseball, first love and the disappearance of his U.S. Army father overseas.

CHRISTIE BRINKLEY HAS FANS MISTAKING SUPERMODEL FOR DAUGHTER IN NEW PHOTOS

"I have always been all about family, so I have built my life in a way that my kids. ... I want them independent," Brinkley said. "I want them out there living, doing whatever, but they always tend to come home on weekends, holidays. We all really are big on being together, and I love that.

"It's funny because a lot of moms on Instagram will ask me, 'How do you get your kids to come home so often? Mine are off and about,'" the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl shared. 

"And I think it's just to always let them know they're always welcome back. They can bring their friends, that kind of thing."

The supermodel is often photographed alongside her three grown children — Alexa Ray Joel, 40, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook, 31, and Sailor Brinkley-Cook, 28 — whether they're walking red carpets or stepping out in coordinated looks. Brinkley said their close bond didn't happen by accident but was rooted in the example set by her own parents.

WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY SHARES SECRET TO KEEPING HER FAMILY CLOSE

After losing both of her parents less than two months apart in 2012, Brinkley said she no longer takes family time for granted. Her father, Don Brinkley, died July 14, followed by her mother, Marge Brinkley, on Sept. 9.

"I have always cherished my family time," Brinkley said. "And I think once you lose both of your parents, it becomes more precious because you know that there is a finite time to it. And right now, our family's smaller because I don't have my mom and dad."

Brinkley became visibly emotional before saying, "I always get choked up whenever I talk about them."

Guttenberg is no stranger to Brinkley's heartbreak. He became a caregiver for his father, Stanley Guttenberg, after he developed kidney failure, eventually training to help administer dialysis at home.

"I remember you telling me about your mom and dad, Christie, that you had a little house on your property, and they lived near you, right?" Guttenberg said. "Isn't that wonderful? How lucky you were and are to have them right there. It's priceless, right? ... The greatest thing in the world."

"The best," Brinkley replied. "My parents were always, always so ready to be there for me. Good times, bad times, they were always there, and they always made an effort to be a family. And I think it's so important, and it has given me my happiest moments."

Family continues to be an essential part of Brinkley's life. She shared that Alexa Ray was preparing for a concert that night, while Jack planned to attend the premiere of "American Summer" alongside her.

For Brinkley, the movie's message extends beyond the screen. She believes audiences are craving stories that celebrate family.

"People want to put down their phone and speak to another human face to face," she said. "This [story] takes us back before there were cellphones. And I think that we're going to find people now putting down their cellphones more often and just connecting with loved ones. 

"And that human connection, nothing can replace it. I find that whenever I light a little bonfire in the backyard or at the beach. I always say, 'This is it. This is free. This is simple. And you know what? This is as good as it gets.'

"Just to be able to sit there by the crackling of the fire, the moon coming up, the stars sparkling, the birds chirping, the crickets coming on, the fireflies lighting — that's it," she continued. "That's the best. Slowing down the speed of life, human connections. ... I think those are things that we all want to feel again and again."

"It's better than any Ferrari," Guttenberg said.

Brinkley's love of simple pleasures doesn't stop with family gatherings. She's also an avid birdwatcher, a hobby she believes is making a comeback as more people look to unplug.

"I've always been a birdwatcher," she said. "On my Instagram, I have a bird feeder, and if you go back, you'll see lots and lots of pictures of the birds at my bird feeder. And I was just reading that birdwatching is back in full force for young people, too. People want to connect with nature. They want to get in nature, and it's all part of just that slowing down."

And after raising three children, Brinkley believes that slowing down and making time for family helps keep loved ones coming back home.

item.title: North Carolina Dem Senate candidate added former Bloods gang member to criminal justice task force: report
item.description: Roy Cooper appointed a convicted Bloods gang member to his criminal justice reform task force in 2020, a Washington Free Beacon report reveals.
item.content:encoded:
Roy Cooper, the former Democrat governor of North Carolina now running for Senate, added an ex-member of the notorious Bloods gang to a Racial Equity in Criminal Justice task force in 2020.

In the wake of George Floyd's 2020 death, Cooper created the task force via executive order, The Washington Free Beacon reported.

Cooper, who tapped then-state attorney general turned current Gov. Josh Stein to lead the task force, stocked the panel with a mix of state officials and community activists, including Kerwin Pittman, who was convicted in 2007 of conspiracy to commit murder, serving 14 years in prison for the crime, according to records obtained by the Free Beacon.

Pittman was also identified as a "ranking member of the Bloods" by prosecutors during a murder trial for Bloods member Michael Contrez Jones.

SIX-FIGURE PRIVATE SECURITY BILL FOR TOP DEM SENATE HOPEFUL FUELS GOP HYPOCRISY CLAIMS

Pittman was convicted in a 2006 drive-by-shooting of 19-year-old Jamel Amiens Jeffreys, the Free Beacon reported.

Pittman defended his involvement in the task force and argued his past actions were the result of poor judgment as a teenager.

"I was asked to contribute to conversations about criminal justice reform because of both my lived experience and the work I was doing in communities," Pittman told the Free Beacon. 

"I have never hidden my past. The gang involvement and criminal conduct you reference occurred when I was a teenager and young man at or before the age of 19. I am now 39 years old.

ONE YEAR AFTER IRYNA ZARUTSKA MURDER, VIOLENT CRIMES FUEL NORTH CAROLINA PUBLIC SAFETY DEBATE

"I made decisions as a young person that had serious consequences, including spending more than a decade incarcerated."

Pittman, according to his LinkedIn profile, worked at the time of the task force's creation for Emancipate NC, an organization which, as the Free Beacon reported, has often called for the abolition of police, writing that "maintaining white supremacy has always been the goal of policing" in a 2023 company blog post.

Cooper, who is running for Senate against former Republican National Committee Chairman Michael Whatley, referenced his opponent's record when asked to comment on the Free Beacon story.

DEM SENATE HOPEFUL PIVOTS ON DATA CENTERS AS RISING POWER COSTS COLLIDE WITH CAMPAIGN

"While Roy spent his career putting rapists and violent criminals behind bars and signing tough-on-crime laws as governor, Michael Whatley spent his appointing a convicted child sex predator who served six years in prison and spent over a decade as a registered sex offender to a top role within the North Carolina Republican Party that gave him access to events with children," the Cooper campaign told Fox News Digital in a statement.

Pittman and the Whatley campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: Your daily coffee habit could be taking a toll on your bones, new study suggests
item.description: A Flinders University study links high coffee consumption to lower bone density in postmenopausal women, while tea's catechins may promote bone health.
item.content:encoded:
If you’re a woman who regularly reaches for coffee throughout the day, you may want to think twice about that next cup — or consider switching to tea.

Researchers at Flinders University reported in a study published in the journal Nutrients that high coffee consumption may be associated with lower bone mineral density (BMD) in older, postmenopausal women.

The scientists analyzed coffee and tea consumption among 9,704 women age 65 and older over a 10-year period. During that time, they also measured participants’ BMD at the femoral neck and hip, areas where osteoporosis-related fractures commonly occur.

The researchers found that drinking tea was associated with higher total hip BMD, while drinking more than five cups of coffee per day was associated with lower BMD.

COFFEE MAY HAVE POWERFUL EFFECT ON LIVER HEALTH, MAJOR STUDY SUGGESTS

Moderate coffee consumption — about two to three cups a day — was not associated with negative effects on bone health.

The study also identified differences based on other health and lifestyle factors. Coffee consumption was associated with lower femoral neck BMD among women with higher alcohol intake, while the positive association between tea and bone density was more pronounced among women with obesity.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The researchers wrote that osteoporosis, which is characterized by low BMD, "is a major global public health concern affecting individuals across all ages, genders and ethnicities."

About one in three women and one in five men age 50 and older worldwide experience osteoporosis-related fractures, according to the study.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Women face a particularly high risk because they generally have lower bone mass and experience accelerated bone loss after menopause.

In the U.S., the number of adults age 50 and older with low BMD in the hip or spine is projected to increase by 17.2 million by 2030, adding to the healthcare costs and long-term disability associated with osteoporosis-related fractures, the researchers noted.

The scientists wrote that they studied the relationship between coffee and tea and bone health because dietary factors play a "crucial role in the prevention of noncommunicable disease and may influence bone health," and these are two of the most widely consumed beverages globally.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Study co-author Ryan Liu told ScienceDaily "compounds called catechins, abundant in tea, may promote bone formation and slow bone breakdown."

"Coffee’s caffeine content, by contrast, has been shown in laboratory studies to interfere with calcium absorption and bone metabolism, though these effects are small and can be offset by adding milk," Liu said.

"Our results don't mean you need to give up coffee or start drinking tea by the gallon," Liu added. "But they do suggest that moderate tea consumption could be one simple way to support bone health and that very high coffee intake might not be ideal, especially for women who drink alcohol."

"This study offers an interesting look at how everyday beverages might relate to bone health, but the findings should be interpreted with caution," Lisa Young, registered dietitian and adjunct professor of nutrition at New York University, told Fox News Digital.

"Because it followed women over time without assigning them to drink coffee or tea, it can only show associations, not prove that coffee weakens bones or that tea strengthens them."

The study had limitations, including differences in participants’ lifestyles, its focus on bone density rather than fractures and relatively small effects seen mainly in older women, Young noted. 

Symptoms of osteoporosis and early bone loss include back pain, loss of height over time and stooped posture, according to the Mayo Clinic.

"The bottom line for the public is reassuring: Moderate coffee intake appears fine, and there is no need to switch drinks for the sake of your bones," Young said. 

"The most proven ways to protect bone health remain getting enough calcium and vitamin D, staying physically active and avoiding smoking and excess alcohol," she added. 

"With that said, I do make a case for moderate amounts of coffee for good health. Too much of anything is never a good thing."

item.title: Fighter jet crashes at air show, killing 2 pilots with thousands of spectators watching
item.description: Video captured a Phantom F-4 jet crashing into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver at Tanagra Air Force Base as thousands witnessed it.
item.content:encoded:
A day at an air show turned fatal Saturday when a Greek air force jet crashed north of Athens as thousands of spectators watched.

Both pilots were killed in the crash at Tanagra Air Force Base, but no civilians were hurt.

The twin-seat Phantom F-4 jet flew into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver just meters above the ground.

EIGHT BELIEVED DEAD AFTER B-52 CRASHES SHORTLY AFTER TAKEOFF FROM EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE

"The sense of grief is widespread, and our thoughts are with the families of the two pilots we lost," Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said. "It is a reminder of the daily danger faced by Greece’s aviators, who remain on constant standby to protect Greece's skies."

The jet burst into flames on impact, sending up a large plume of black smoke, prompting 11 water-dropping planes and helicopters to assist 85 firefighters in extinguishing the blaze.

11 SKYDIVERS, ONE PILOT KILLED IN MISSOURI PLANE CRASH NEAR AIRPORT

Video of the crash showed a second ball of fire nearby as the plane broke apart.

The bodies of the pilots were eventually recovered.

"We were all stunned. It hadn't been airborne for more than three minutes," an eyewitness told ERT, Greece’s state-owned broadcaster.

The crash happened during the country’s annual Athens Flying Week.

The organizers canceled the rest of the events after the incident, and the area was evacuated.

"It is with deep sadness that I learned of the death of the two officers of the Hellenic Air Force, who lost their lives in the tragic accident that occurred during the air show at Tanagra Air Base," Cyprus' Defense Minister Vasilis Palmas said, adding he had called Nikos Dendias, Greece’s Minister of National Defense.

AIR FORCE IDENTIFIES 8 CREW MEMBERS KILLED IN B-52 STRATOFORTRESS CRASH AT EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE

The air force has declared three days of mourning in the country.

In May, two jets collided during an air show in Idaho, but the pilots were able to safely eject.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Indiana's mascot starts the season with an absolute heater that puts other mascots to shame
item.description: The Indiana Hoosiers mascot Hoosier the Bison zip-lined into Memorial Stadium, then drove an IndyCar around the field during the pregame spectacle.
item.content:encoded:
The Indiana Hoosiers began their quest to build on a magical 2025 season that ended with a national championship.

It remains to be seen how the year will turn out, but one thing is already certain: their mascot, Hoosier the Bison, will be bringing it every single weekend.

The Hoosiers reintroduced a bison mascot for the first time in sixty years last season, and the timing proved to be perfect.

MINOR LEAGUE PLAYER GETS SMOKED BY A SCOOTER-RIDING MASCOT IN WILD MOMENT CAUGHT ON CAMERA

For his debut, Hoosier skydived into Memorial Stadium.

Ripping a speed star like Keanu and Patrick Swayze in "Point Break" is tough to beat for a mascot debut. It was easily the best since Gritty threatened to kill the Penguins mascot.

So, for his sophomore season, Hoosier went with the zip line.

Not bad, not bad at all.

But if that was the extent of the mascottery, it left a little on the table.

...Wait, what's that?

I'm being told he also drove around the field in an IndyCar while the marching band performed.

Are you not entertained?!

HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL

That's one of those "The European mind can't comprehend it" moments.

"Why is that cow driving a racecar on the pitch while the band is playing?"

First of all, it's a "bison" and a "field," and secondly, it's because it's college football, Üter.

What a start. I love to see restraint like that on display. Hoosier didn't have to knock everyone's proverbial socks off with the zip line because he knew that there was an open-wheel race car waiting in the wings.

You don't see that out of these modern mascots; usually only the blue bloods have the experience to know that you don't want to give away everything with your opener.

Fortunately, mascots aren't getting poached by way of NIL (not yet, but give it time) because after that performance, there's no doubt some schools with big checkbooks would be circling him like sharks around fresh chum.

item.title: Indiana QB Josh Hoover delivers the greatest 'football guy' moment of the season so far

item.content:encoded:

Three plays after the penalty, with blood pouring down his nose, dripping from his chinstrap and facemask, Hoover delivered a dart to arguably his favorite target, wide receiver Charlie Becker for a 9-yard touchdown.

item.title: John Harbaugh and Jaxson Dart aim to pull the New York Giants out of the NFC East basement
item.description: John Harbaugh and Jaxson Dart lead the New York Giants' massive reset, but questions linger about a defense that bled big plays last season.
item.content:encoded:
With John Harbaugh taking over as head coach and Jaxson Dart entering his first full year as the starter, the New York Giants aim to reset after multiple years of struggle.

But with championship-winning head coach Harbaugh stepping in to take the helm and second-year quarterback Dart taking over as the full-time leader under center, New York is aiming to prove that its structural reset is complete and that they can climb out of the NFC East basement.

The Giants suffered through a miserable 2025 campaign, finishing 4–13 and missing the postseason for the third consecutive year. New York showed flashes of an explosive future after rookie first-round pick Jaxson Dart took over in Week 4, bringing dynamic dual-threat playmaking and pulling off upset wins over the Los Angeles Chargers and Dallas Cowboys.

GIANTS' DRAFT PICK HAS INTENSE JAXSON DART MESSAGE: 'I’M READY TO DIE FOR YOU'

However, catastrophic defensive breakdowns and an inability to protect leads defined the season, as New York lost seven single-possession games and blew five double-digit leads. The mid-season firing of Brian Daboll signaled the end of the previous regime and set up a massive front-office overhaul entering the winter.

To fix the organizational culture, the biggest splash was the hiring cycle, luring longtime Ravens head coach John Harbaugh to East Rutherford, and then bringing in Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator to design a system around Dart.

In free agency and trade markets, the front office aggressively supplemented the roster with proven talent. They signed physical Baltimore tight end Isaiah Likely, while bolstering the defense with cornerback Paulson Adebo and safety Jevon Holland. On the subtraction side, New York parted ways with several depth pieces across the front seven and secondary while re-shaping the wide receiver room to prioritize fast, versatile weapons.

There is reason for cautious, high-ceiling optimism when evaluating New York’s roster makeup. The offense relies heavily on Dart’s dual-threat versatility, backed by star wideout Malik Nabers on the perimeter (who is returning from injury) and the tight-end tandem of Isaiah Likely and Theo Johnson.

With an upgraded offensive line anchored by Andrew Thomas, the run game with Cam Skattebo (also returning from injury) and Tyrone Tracy Jr. should provide crucial balance. It will be up to the offensive line to find a way to make it work, though. They are ranked by PFF at 23rd in the league.

Defensively, the front seven boasts legitimate star power with edge rusher Brian Burns coming off an All-Pro-caliber campaign alongside Kayvon Thibodeaux and rookie pass-rush talent. With Adebo and Holland reinforcing a secondary that bled big plays last fall, the unit has the talent to transition from a liability into a formidable group. They will still need to win in the trenches, and their team is ranked 21st on the defensive line.

I think under Harbaugh, you will see the Giants have an instant improvement. I’m not expecting them to win the division (I have the Cowboys). I do think they should get to seven wins, and potentially eight. Skattebo and Dart combined to provide some excitement, and if Nabers comes back healthy, this should be a fun team to watch. I still have a lot of questions about their defense, but the reality is that Harbaugh should show his impact in that aspect more than any other area. item.title: Jeff Foxworthy reveals how 'redneck' insult inspired decades of comedy
item.description: Jeff Foxworthy reveals why he brought back his iconic "redneck" jokes after 20 years for his Fox Nation special "The Joke's on Me," streaming now.
item.content:encoded:
Jeff Foxworthy turned an insult into a compliment when someone criticized where he came from.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 67-year-old actor and comedian discussed his new stand-up special, "The Joke's on Me," and recalled the time someone called him a "redneck" and how he turned what was meant to be an insult into a compliment.

He explained that "one of the nicest compliments" someone once gave him was commending his ability to turn what "was supposed to be an insult ... into a badge of honor."

DAVE CHAPPELLE SAYS HE’S CONSIDERING REVISITING ‘CHAPPELLE’S SHOW’ DECADES AFTER WALKING AWAY

"I said, 'Well, that's cool, because when people get offended, they act like if you gave rednecks a billion dollars, they wouldn't be rednecks,'" he said. 

"I said they would still be rednecks. They would just have bigger boats, bigger trucks. I mean, more things to shoot at. They're happy with who they are. And I've always got asked, ‘How do you come up with that?’ And I'm like. There's no research going on. It's my family and my friend group that trust me."

Foxworthy first began telling jokes about rednecks in the late '80s, and found them to be successful, so he continued telling them, even closing his 1990 special with one.

He explained that "they were easy to remember" and said they would always "get a laugh." After telling the jokes on stage for a while, he "thought, well people are tired of this" and stopped telling them.

"The last time I did them onstage was during the Blue Collar Comedy Tour" in 2003, he said.

WATCH: Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up.

After more than 20 years of staying away from the jokes, Foxworthy felt like it was time to bring them back. He recalled telling the crowd, "I hadn't done these in 20 years, but I'm thinking about for this special, bringing them back.

"I said that because when I said that if you've ever peed in the pool, the entire audience went, 'You might be a redneck.' And I went, 'Oh, wow, this stuck to people's bones, you know?'" he said. 

"And I say, ‘Well, what if I did some to close, if that was my first special, and all these years later, this is my last.’ It kind of seemed like a nice little way to put a bow on it."

He then went back and looked at all the redneck jokes he had written over the years, "and pulled out a bunch of them" to try at his next gig at a comedy club.

"It was like, I never stopped doing them," he said. "It was like going back 35 years, which was really cool for me. It's like one of your babies. You bring it back out and people go, 'Oh, we still love it.'"

WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy explains why he stopped telling 'redneck' jokes

Foxworthy's latest comedy special, "The Joke's on Me" began streaming on Fox Nation in June. Unlike other comedy specials, this one gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at the joke-writing process that goes into creating a special.

The comedian told Fox News Digital he was inspired to create the unique special after watching a documentary about the Beatles and realizing that "seeing the process didn't take anything away from the finished product," but rather made it better "because you saw the struggle that went into creating that."

When Fox Nation approached him with the offer to do a stand-up special, he pitched them the behind-the-scenes idea.

"I said, 'But if you're willing to try something different, if you will show me note cards in hand, going into a club on a Tuesday night or a Wednesday night and just throwing these thoughts out.' Because one of the things that still fascinates me after over 40 years about stand-up is I still don't know what people are gonna laugh at," he said.

"You would think after 40 years, I would know. Now, I'll go in there with an idea, 'Oh, this is really funny.' And then nobody laughs. Or I'll have a card where I think this is so stupid, I'm embarrassed to say it, and you throw it out there and everybody's beaten the tables laughing. And you're like, really? And, so, I wanted to show that. And Fox Nation was the first place that ever said, 'OK, we'll do it.'"

Foxworthy has hinted that this could be his last stand-up special but assures fans that doesn't mean he will never perform on a stage again.

He told Fox News Digital he has reached a point in his life where the time he would rather spend with his grandkids or on his tractor.

"I've been on the road nonstop," he added. "I laugh at my music friends when they say they're on tour. I said, 'Well, tour implies it stops. At some point,' I said, 'I've been on tour since 1984.' It just never stopped. I still love stand-up. I just don't know that I'm willing. And, to be honest, I'm not sure I can do anything any better than this, which just feels like a good place to stop."
